podcast.body: Released in June 1979, this disco track became Chic's second number one song, topping the Billboard Hot 100 by August 18th and reaching number three on the disco chart. Nile Rogers noted that he and Bernard Edwards recognized it as "the perfect hip hop record" due to its extended breakdown, which could accommodate long rhymes. Barry Crocker, reviewing for The New York Rocker in 1980, described its appeal as coming from a "raunchy pulse" and a "gut level instinct," despite its lush orchestrations. The song's bassline was compared to a "jungle drum" and its handclap to a "heartbeat lifeline." It is ranked number 220 on Rolling Stone's list of the top 500 songs of all time, largely due to its extensive sampling. "Good Times" is recognized for its profound influence on hip hop, with its DNA woven into the genre, and its baseline forming the core of "Rapper's Delight." "The breakdown took so long to develop that they could have rhymes that could go on forever."
